sec: Introduction and classification of diabetes mellitus

items.q: The common presenting symptom written at the opening of this page is:
items.exp: The page names hyperglycemia as the common presenting symptom and lists endocrinopathy as the most common association. (Book p917)

items.q: The classification notes identify ___ as the common presenting symptom.
items.exp: Hyperglycemia is written as the common presenting symptom. (Book p917)

items.q: Match the following classification to the description — 1) Type 1 DM 2) Type 2 DM 3) Hybrid DM 4) GDM … A) Immune-mediated pancreatic destruction B) Insulin resistance C) Type 1.5 diabetes D) Gestational diabetes mellitus
items.exp: The page defines Type 1 as predominantly immune-mediated pancreatic destruction, Type 2 as insulin resistance, hybrid diabetes as Type 1.5, and GDM as gestational diabetes mellitus. (Book p917)

items.q: Assess the first two classification notes: I Type 1 DM is described as predominantly immune mediated. II Type 2 DM is described as predominantly immune mediated.
items.exp: Type 1 is described as predominantly immune-mediated pancreatic destruction; Type 2 is described through insulin resistance. (Book p917)

items.q: A learner is sorting the note's causes of pancreatic destruction in Type 2 DM. Which pair belongs together in the printed sequence?
items.exp: The Type 2 line links glucotoxicity and lipotoxicity with pancreatic destruction. (Book p917)

items.q: Which is the odd one out among the page's named diabetes categories?
items.exp: Cushing diabetes is not one of the named categories in the classification list on this page; Type 1, Type 2 and hybrid diabetes are listed. (Book p917)

items.q: What percentage range is written beside Type 2 diabetes mellitus?
items.exp: The Type 2 diabetes mellitus entry is annotated with 90–95%. (Book p917)

items.q: A patient is using the artificial-pancreas arrangement shown on the page. Which sequence reflects the printed operation?
opts: Sensor measures glucose, pump calculates insulin, smartphone displays readings and accepts carbohydrate input
Pump measures glucose, sensor injects insulin, smartphone stores ketones
Smartphone measures glucose, sensor gives glucagon, pump records meals
Sensor measures carbohydrates, pump gives saline, smartphone checks C-peptide
items.exp: The artificial-pancreas note describes a skin sensor, wireless transmission to a pump that calculates insulin, and smartphone monitoring with carbohydrate input. (Book p917)

items.q: Match the Type 3 branch to its printed example — 1) Type 3 diabetes 2) Type 3a 3) Type 3c 4) Type 3d … A) Alzheimer’s disease B) Parent category shown above the branches C) Pancreatic diabetes D) Drug-induced diabetes
items.exp: The page shows Type 3 branching to Alzheimer’s disease, Type 3c pancreatic diabetes, and Type 3d drug-induced diabetes. (Book p917)

items.q: Assess the remaining labels: I Type 4 is called mild age-related diabetes. II MODY is expanded as maturity onset diabetes of young.
items.exp: Type 4 is labelled mild age-related diabetes (MARD), and MODY is expanded as maturity onset diabetes of young. (Book p917)

items.q: The Type 4 note links mild age-related diabetes with which immune-cell association?
items.exp: The page places an association with T-regulatory cells below Type 4 mild age-related diabetes. (Book p917)

items.q: The diagram beside Alzheimer’s disease links insulin-degrading enzyme with degradation of insulin and:
items.exp: The Alzheimer’s branch depicts insulin-degrading enzyme and shows degradation of insulin and APO-Ba before APO-Ba accumulation. (Book p917)

items.q: The abbreviation GDM on this page expands to ___.
items.exp: GDM is written as gestational diabetes mellitus in the classification list. (Book p917)
